newsitem.title: INDONESIA: BANK INDONESIA DEFENDS BAND, RUPIAH STABILISES.
newsitem.headline: BANK INDONESIA DEFENDS BAND, RUPIAH STABILISES.

text.p: Bank Indonesia defended its intervention band on Wednesday after the rupiah fell to a historic low, erasing much of the currency's losses by the close of the day, dealers said.
They said the central bank intervened by selling dollars in the spot market although some said the bank was also seen in the one-month forward market.
The rupiah bounced back sharply to 2,620 from a historic low of 2,682 before easing back to 2,650/60 at 0945 GMT at the close of trading in Jakarta. The rupiah opened at 2,643/50.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,644/54 and 2,665/68, respectively.
Bank Indonesia kept its dollar-rupiah intervention band unchanged on Wednesday at 2,378/2,682 but raised its conversion band to 2,629/2,677 from 2,616/2,664 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the market had speculated that the band would be widened or possibly removed altogether after the rupiah plunged before recovering on the intervention.
Dealers said they were not clear how much money the central bank had pumped into the market to calm nervous operators.
"But for sure we are going to see a tightened money market on Friday. The move will result in rupiah scarcity," one said.
The local bank dealer said operators had immediately locked in longer-term liquidity available now.
Dealers said the central bank was trying to defend the band with the help of the short-term interest rate policy.

The bank raised interest rates for bilateral central bank certificates (SBIs) of all maturities by 100 basis points. Overnight rates were raised to 15.0 percent, two-to-six day SBIs to 16.0 percent, one-week to 10.5, two-week to 11.0, one-month to 11.625, three to 11.5, six to 12.125 and one-year to 12.75.
The central bank also remained absent from the short-term securities (SBPUs) market.
The central bank cut its bilateral SBI rates for papers above one-week by 50 basis points last Friday after the foreign exchange market showed signs of stabilisation.
However, renewed pressure spilling over from neighbouring countries knocked the rupiah down further, forcing the central bank to impose a tighter money policy to contain speculation.
Dealers said heavy selling of the rupiah on Wednesday was triggered on contagion effect from the Singapore dollar and the Malaysian ringgit and on comments by a local economist.
Sjahrir, an economist and brokerage firm owner, was quoted in the Kompas daily as saying the market would ultimately decide a fair value for the rupiah.

"According to me, just let the rupiah fall to 2,700 or 2,800. The central bank does not have to do anything. Once they (speculators) realise the central bank hasn't done anything, the dollar is already overvalued," Sjahrir was quoted as saying.
But an economist with one of the country's state-owned banks said the central bank was likely to continue defending the band.
"We all know that there is nothing wrong with the economy or the country's fundamentals. But speculators keep trying. The bank has to give some certainty for the people," the economist said.
"There is little use of pointing to fundamentals. We just have to wait until the storm is over," he said.
Dealers said swap rates remained high as the central bank was seen mainly in the spot market.
Overnight swap was at 1.05/1.25 and tom/next at 1.5/1.8.
One local bank dealer said offshore operators were seen biddish in one-week and one-month swaps, pushing them to end at 7.5/8.5 and 30.0/40.0 points, respectively.
Two-month swap was at 55.0/61.0, three at 72.0/78.0 and six at 130.0/136.0 points.
Overnight money was last at 20.0/25.0 percent.
The central bank had intervened last month in the forward market with some one billion dollars.
